pages.text:
Maya loved looking at the stars from her bedroom window. She often wondered if someone lived on other planets.

One night, she heard a loud crash in her backyard.

She ran outside and found a small silver robot sitting beside a strange spaceship.

“Hello,” the robot said. “My name is Ziko. I came from Mars.”

Maya could hardly believe her ears.

“Are you really from Mars?” she asked.

Ziko nodded. “Yes. But my spaceship is broken, and I need your help.”

Maya smiled. “Don't worry. We'll fix it together.”

Ziko showed Maya a small glowing machine.

“This power crystal is damaged,” he explained. “Without it, I cannot return home.”

Maya remembered that her father kept old electronic parts in his workshop.

Together, they searched through the boxes and found a small piece that looked similar to the broken part.

Maya carefully connected it to Ziko's machine.

Suddenly, the robot's eyes began to glow.

Beep! Beep!

“My spaceship is working!” Ziko shouted happily.

Before leaving, Ziko showed Maya a holographic picture of Mars.

Maya was amazed by the red mountains and enormous valleys.

“Maybe one day, humans will visit Mars,” she said.

“Maybe you will be one of them,” Ziko replied.

Ziko climbed into his spaceship.

“Thank you, Maya,” he said. “You helped me return home.”

The spaceship rose slowly into the sky and disappeared among the stars.

Maya went back to her room and looked through her telescope.

Suddenly, a tiny red light flashed near Mars.

Her computer made a soft sound.

Message received:

“Hello from Mars, Maya. Keep looking at the stars.”

Maya smiled.

From that night onward, she never looked at the sky in the same way again.

She knew that somewhere beyond the stars, her new friend Ziko was waiting for her next adventure.

The End.

title: The Princess and the Magic Star
author: Saru Rai

pages.text:
Once upon a time, there lived a kind princess named Elara in a beautiful kingdom. Every night, a magical golden star shone above her castle and filled the kingdom with light.

One evening, the star suddenly disappeared. The flowers lost their colors, the rivers stopped sparkling, and the kingdom became dark.

The King was very worried. “Without the magic star, our kingdom will lose its beauty,” he said.

Princess Elara decided to find the missing star. She packed some food, took a little lantern, and walked into the enchanted forest.

Deep inside the forest, Elara met a tiny fairy named Willow.

“Why are you here, Princess?” asked Willow.

“I am searching for the golden star to save my kingdom,” Elara replied.

The fairy smiled and pointed toward a tall mountain. “A lonely dragon has taken the star. He lives inside a cave at the top of that mountain.”

Elara continued her journey until she reached the cave. Inside, she found the dragon sitting beside the glowing star.

“Please return the star,” Elara said gently. “My kingdom needs its light.”

The dragon looked sad. “I took it because I was lonely. I wanted someone to visit me.”

Elara felt sorry for the dragon. Instead of becoming angry, she promised to visit him and be his friend.

The dragon was happy to hear Elara's promise. He gently gave her the golden star.

Elara carried it back to the castle and placed it on the highest tower. Immediately, golden light spread across the kingdom. The flowers bloomed, the rivers sparkled, and the people cheered with happiness.

The King hugged his daughter proudly.

“You saved our kingdom with your courage and kindness,” he said.

From that day onward, Elara visited the dragon regularly. The dragon was no longer lonely, and the kingdom remained bright and beautiful.

The End.

A cute little fox named Milo standing at the entrance of an enchanted forest at night, looking at a huge glowing moon. Fireflies floating around him, colorful mushrooms, tall magical trees, soft blue and purple night lighting, children's storybook illustration, cute and friendly style, no text.

Milo was a small orange fox who lived with his mother near a quiet forest. He was curious about everything around him. Every morning, he explored the trees, smelled the flowers, and watched the birds flying across the sky.

But there was one place he had never visited—the Moonlit Forest.

One evening, Milo saw a strange silver light coming from deep inside the forest.

“Where is that light coming from?” he wondered.

His mother had always told him, “Never go too far into the forest after sunset.”

Milo looked at the glowing light again.

His curiosity became stronger.

Milo carefully walked between the trees.

The forest looked completely different at night. Tiny fireflies danced above the grass, and the leaves sparkled under the moonlight.

Suddenly, Milo heard a soft voice.

“Hello?”

Milo stopped.

“Who said that?”

A small white owl flew down from a tree.

“My name is Luna,” said the owl. “Why are you here?”

“I followed the strange light,” Milo replied.

Luna looked worried.

“That light belongs to the Moon Crystal. It has disappeared from the forest.”

“What happens if the crystal doesn't come back?” Milo asked.

“The forest will slowly lose its magic,” Luna explained.

The flowers would stop glowing. The trees would become weak, and the animals would lose their special abilities.

Milo knew he had to help.

“I'll find the crystal,” he said bravely.

Milo and Luna followed a trail of silver dust until they reached a wide river.

On the other side, they saw tiny footprints.

“The crystal must have gone that way!” Milo shouted.

But there was no bridge.

Milo looked around and noticed several large logs floating near the riverbank.

Milo carefully stepped onto a log.

“Be careful!” Luna called.

The log moved from side to side.

Milo took a deep breath and kept walking.

Step by step, he reached the other side.

“You did it!” Luna cheered.

Milo smiled proudly.

The silver trail led them to a dark cave.

Milo was frightened.

“I don't think I can go inside,” he whispered.

Luna smiled.

“Being brave doesn't mean you aren't afraid. It means you keep going even when you are afraid.”

Milo took a deep breath and entered the cave.

Deep inside the cave, Milo saw something shining.

It was the Moon Crystal!

But it was trapped underneath a large rock.

Milo pushed the rock.

Nothing happened.

He pushed again.

Still nothing.

Then Luna called the forest animals for help.

A much-anticipated debut by Aida Salazar. Celi Rivera’s life swirls with questions. About her changing body. Her first attraction to a boy. And her best friend’s exploration of what it means to be genderfluid. But most of all, her mother’s insistence she have a moon ceremony when her first period arrives. It’s an ancestral Mexica ritual that Mima and her community have reclaimed, but Celi promises she will NOT be participating. Can she find the power within herself to take a stand for who she wants to be? [middle grade, ages 8 and up]

title: Mr.Worry
author: Holly L. Niner, illustrated by Greg Swearingen

pages.text: Kevin can't get to sleep at night until he does many things. He straightens his chair and the books on his desk. He asks his mother questions he already knows the answers to. He checks under his bed for a light he knows isn't there, and then, a minute later, he checks again. Kevin knows these actions don't make sense; he wants to stop, but the worry thoughts keep coming. When his parents realize that Kevin has too many worries, they take him to talk to a therapist. She tells Kevin and his parents that Kevin has a condition called obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and that, more importantly, he can be helped.

Here is a collection of short pieces of University Life that Clark, the Narrator, experienced after transferring from State College. These brief glimpses of campus life are some of the more poignant moments that Clark narrates after losing himself after a break-up from a long-term relationship, and then purposely losing himself in a big city. The slow recovery of self-esteem is hit and miss, and many traps and setbacks along the way can and did occur. There were also a variety of diversions that were, if not at least a cause of some levity, then surely some of the most unlikely events he ever expected to experience.

But all the hassle helps start the recovery of a self and a Soul that was once damaged beyond apparent repair.There is no fluid continuity to these stories, except by an effort to order them somewhat sequentially and to present them through the eyes of the Narrator.Sometimes the stories may appear to overlap, or double back to the past.Sometimes the same roots are common and important to several stories.Hopefully, there is a unique connection to a root event that gives clearer insight into the new incident.With the understanding that there will be gaps in time between some stories and short intervals between others; this reflects how time can sometimes stand still - due to studies and routines - or move more dynamically, due to events happening in rapid succession. The stories cover a minimum four years in the mid-to-later-70s and (mostly) at this university and its vicinity.

The stories have been fictionalized and do not claim to accurately depict any actual events or characters as they may or may not have happened, or as campus hearsay would have it, or cross-collecting research across several colleges may have had them play out.What happened in the 70s - happened. No excuse will be made for other character's actions, the events as depicted, nor the Narrator's own thoughts and reactions. No attempt to be politically correct is maintained here. Perhaps some of these events should have been left in the past; but nevertheless, they unfold in the following stories of the Narrator's herky-jerky college life.
Once upon a time, in a dense green forest, stood a magical treehouse filled with countless books.
Today, the magical window pointed toward a land of golden deserts and whispering winds.
As they climbed down, a friendly golden fox appeared, guiding them toward the ancient oasis.
